findings.title: Legacy-branch selection changes an existing 400 contract for partial legacy requests
findings.location: Endpoint design -> guard order, step 2 (Decide the path)
findings.problem: The adapter path is taken 'when GameSystem/Ruleset are absent'. A legacy request with canonicalJson + gameSystem but a missing ruleset currently returns 400 'ruleset is required.' Under the proposed routing it falls into the adapter branch, skips the ruleset guard, and returns 200/other instead of 400. The 'legacy contract preserved' claim only holds for fully-formed legacy bodies, and the described regression test (which posts a complete legacy body) would not catch it.
findings.fix: Treat the request as legacy whenever source is absent AND (GameSystem present OR Ruleset present) so partial legacy bodies still get their 'ruleset is required.'/'gameSystem is required.' 400. Route to adapter only when source is present OR BOTH GameSystem AND Ruleset are absent. Add an integration case asserting { canonicalJson, gameSystem, no ruleset, no source } still returns 400 'ruleset is required.'

findings.title: ApplyMappingPathAcceptanceTests payload and frontend confirm flow omit the required FieldMappingEntry.SourceFieldName
findings.location: Test plan -> ApplyMappingPathAcceptanceTests.cs; Frontend confirm flow
findings.problem: The design submits mappings as { canonicalFieldPath, value }, but the real contract is FieldMappingEntry(string SourceFieldName, string CanonicalFieldPath, string Value) with SourceFieldName as a required positional parameter. A two-field object will not construct. The frontend synthesizes FieldMappingEntry[] from review.mappedFields but never states what SourceFieldName each entry carries.
findings.fix: Specify the full entry shape in the test plan: new FieldMappingEntry(SourceFieldName: <path or label>, CanonicalFieldPath: <path>, Value: <representative in-range value>). State in the frontend section that each synthesized entry sets SourceFieldName to the mapped path or source label so the submission is well-formed. (ApplyFieldMappingsAsync skips entries whose CanonicalFieldPath is blank but does not validate SourceFieldName, so any non-null label is acceptable.)

findings.title: Acceptance-test representative values must respect ParseIntMapping range limits
findings.problem: ParseIntMapping enforces per-path ranges (abilities 1..30, AC 0..99, hp/maxhp 0..9999, speed 0..999, initiative -20..20, proficiencyBonus 0..10, level >= 1). A single flat value could fail range checks for reasons unrelated to path acceptance, masking the real assertion.
findings.fix: Give the acceptance test a per-path representative-value table (ability=15, AC=15, hp=20, maxhp=20, speed=30, initiative=2, proficiencyBonus=2, level=1, string paths='x').

findings.title: Numeric MappedFields values should be bare integers to survive ParseIntMapping cleaning
findings.problem: ParseIntMapping splits on space/'(' and TrimEnd('f','t','.') to handle '30 ft.'. A mapper emitting a numeric string with a unit or stripped trailing char could be silently altered at save. Mappers read via TryGetInt32/TryGetDouble so this is unlikely, but the contract is not stated.
findings.fix: Add to the standing mapper rule: numeric MappedFields values are emitted as bare base-10 integer strings (no units/suffixes) so ParseIntMapping passes them through unchanged.

findings.title: Confirm the new PersistDraftFromCanonicalAsync does not reuse the PDF helper's Unknown-stub fallback
findings.problem: The real PersistDraftFromExtractionAsync falls back to a minimal Unknown/level-1 character on ArgumentException, discarding mapped data (verified). The new sibling helper is sound, but the design should ensure it does not accidentally inherit that destructive fallback branch.
findings.fix: Explicitly state the new helper persists the partial CanonicalJson as-is with a warning and never constructs an Unknown stub.
